purpose: Routing index for the literature on the laptop and its QWERTY keyboard as a performed musical instrument: melodic key-mapping, rhythmic tapping, typing-as-music, laptop ensembles, the liveness critique, and computers booted into instruments. Built to locate notepat and AC Native OS inside that field.
posture: Index and citation only. Nothing is mirrored into the repo. Peer-reviewed PDFs are linked at their proceedings URL; products and vernacular sites are cited as evidence of practice, never as authority.

checked_key.true: the primary page (proceedings PDF, publisher page, project page) was retrieved during a platter pass and the citation details were read off it
checked_key.false: written from a secondary mention; wants a verification pass before a paper leans on it

search_route: Exa via the ac-web-search MCP (AC-owned, no query logs). 30 queries, 2026-11-02. See README.md for the query list.

shelves.typewriter: Typing as percussion before the computer.
shelves.note-entry: The QWERTY keyboard as a note-entry device: trackers, DAW musical typing, web pianos, the AWSED convention.
shelves.vernacular: Typed-letter notation communities (Virtual Piano / Roblox sheets).
shelves.ensembles: Laptop orchestras and commodity-device ensembles that play the machine's own inputs.
shelves.mappings: Named mapping logics for keys to pitch: positional, harmonic, isomorphic, ASCII, frequency, fretboard.
shelves.typing-music: Typed text as the musical gesture: text-driven instruments, typing toys, letters as operators.
shelves.liveness: The laptop-performance liveness critique and its empirical follow-ups.
shelves.rhythm-latency: Tapped rhythm entry, timing studies, latency budgets, rollover and velocity limits of keyboards.
shelves.instrument-os: Computers booted into instruments or media studios: embedded boxes and live distributions.
shelves.theory: Design theory for digital instruments that the positioning leans on.
